name: SN Kestrel Hover-Bike
description: A single-seat hover-bike that combines a motorcycle form factor with anti-grav lift and turbofan thrust. The Kestrel is the vehicle freelancers dream about and corporate couriers actually ride. Fast, agile, capable of weaving between buildings at terrifying speeds. The handling requires skill that takes years to develop — rookie Kestrel riders have a life expectancy measured in weeks.
propulsion: Anti-grav lift, dual turbofan thrust, electric backup
autonomy: Manual flight, stability assist, terrain-following radar
armament: None standard. Weapon hardpoints available on security variant.
common_usage: Corporate couriers, security pursuit, freelancer operations, aerial racing.
story_hooks: A Kestrel pilot discovers their bike's terrain-following radar is mapping something underneath the city that isn't on any geological survey
Stolen Kestrels are being modified with military firmware and used for coordinated aerial strikes on corporate convoys
physical_description: The Kestrel's frame is a skeletal lattice of scuffed titanium-alloy tubing, its once-sleek gunmetal finish worn to dull gray by rain and wind. Dual turbofan intakes flank the rider's seat like gills, their housings streaked with oxidation and carbon scoring. Anti-grav emitters hum beneath a weathered composite fairing that's been patched and re-welded more times than most riders remember, its original obsidian black faded to charcoal in places where thermal stress has bleached the polymer.
